paragraphs: RedZone Robotics sells robotic sewer inspection, large-diameter cleaning, and asset management for underground wastewater infrastructure. Robots carrying cameras and sensors are sent into pipes to perform pipeline and sewer assessments. The data collected is uploaded to cloud-based software that the customer accesses to assess an entire pipeline and decide on maintenance.

The pages date the company to 1987 and say it pivoted in 2003 to focus exclusively on wastewater, beginning work with the City of Pittsburgh on a tool for inspecting large-diameter pipe. Later development produced Vertue, described as a vertical manhole inspection unit providing customers with comprehensive asset data. Services listed run from small and mid-sized pipe to large-diameter MSI inspection, siphons, and interceptors.

Buyers named on the pages are asset managers at large and small municipalities and agencies, along with regional and national engineering firms. The employment page adds contractors and engineering firms across North America to that list.

quote.text: Healthier, safer, stronger communities, one pipe at a time.
